findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:41-65,119-132 and packages/main/src/handlers/doctor.ts:279-286,490-494 — HIGH: generated-token storage has no lifecycle cleanup or doctor inspection/repair, despite the ratified contract R3 requiring storage ownership, cleanup, and doctor visibility. The writer publishes directly to the final path with flag wx; a partial/corrupt final file is treated as unreadable, then every retry gets EEXIST and rethrows forever. Repro on current dist: create one token, replace its JSON with {partial, then call readOrCreateOwnerSessionToken for the same dimensions => ERROR_CODE=EEXIST. This can permanently brick a supported generated-token boundary until an undocumented manual deletion, and tokens otherwise accumulate without expiry/owner-scoped cleanup.

packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:1682-1687 — HIGH: buildCanonicalHostRuntimeEnv re-adds process.env.LATTICE_SESSION_ID whenever envAllowlist contains it, without honoring envDenylist. This bypasses buildRequiredCommandEnv deny precedence and can propagate the parent owner identity into a reviewer child even under an explicit deny policy, collapsing role isolation. Repro on current dist with both lists containing LATTICE_SESSION_ID returns DENYLIST_RESULT=must-stay-denied instead of absent. Preserve explicit override only when allowlisted AND not denied, with a regression for conflicting policy entries.

packages/main/src/core/owner-session-adapters.ts:26-31,63-68 and 130-138 never consume the real Codex task signal CODEX_THREAD_ID and there is no direct Codex wrapper/adapter injection path for LATTICE_OWNER_SESSION_ADAPTER_TASK plus AGENT. In this live Codex task, the environment has CODEX_THREAD_ID but none of CODEX_SESSION_ID/OPENAI_SESSION_ID/TERM_SESSION_ID/LATTICE_AGENT; `env -u LATTICE_SESSION_ID node bin/lattice.js session_brief` therefore reports `[derived-ppid]`. WHY: the shipped path still requires the same manual LATTICE_SESSION_ID workaround and does not solve cross-shell self-lock for the ordinary Codex owner task, despite CHK-001/002 claiming supported adapter stability. Add a validated direct-host bridge that maps the actual durable Codex task signal plus a policy-distinct main/agent role into the canonical composite, with child-shell propagation and a real CLI regression proving two PPIDs keep one id while another task/role differs.

docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:397-404 and 445-461 require a post-implementation R5 run on at least two real hosts and explicitly state that pre-implementation document reviews do not satisfy it. CHK-002 currently binds every supported-host intent only to deterministic logic/smoke tests on a175883c, while the two real-host records in CHK-004 are pre-runtime document reviews. WHY: the story cannot yet claim that the implemented Codex/Claude/agy bridges work in their real launch environments, and the missing real-host run is exactly where the live Codex-variable mismatch escaped. Run the final implementation on two independent real providers (including the actual direct owner-task path), bind exact post-implementation HEAD/material/storyFiles hashes, and keep degraded ppid as the required negative control.

packages/main/src/tasks/story-owner-lease-smoke.ts:102-440 — HIGH coverage gap: CHK-002 binds every must intent to a same-process resolver/env-builder smoke, but the required cross-process contract is not exercised. The test directly calls resolveSessionIdentity/buildCanonicalHostRuntimeEnv and intercepts console.warn; it never spawns the required nested child shells, never invokes session_brief or doctor through the CLI, and never scans child stdout/stderr/activity/evidence for provider sentinels. packages/main/src/tasks/cli-surface-smoke.ts contains no owner-session assertions and is unchanged in this story despite being cited by the evidence. packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:120-130 also adds wx/EEXIST race recovery without a concurrent-writer regression. WHY: the shipped failure occurs across shell/process boundaries, so same-process helper PASS can miss lost child env, cache/reset, CLI rendering, warning-before-write, disclosure, and two-writer token divergence. Add bounded focused regressions that (1) spawn nested provider child processes for Codex/Claude/agy/fake identities and assert stable task/role isolation plus exact session_brief/doctor/pre-mutation diagnostics and redaction, (2) exercise blank explicit override and deliberate allowlisted override through the spawned boundary, (3) race two generated-token creators for one scope and prove one stable token with scoped separation, and (4) retain existing takeover/lifecycle consumer checks. Rebind only the intents actually asserted.

docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:397-404 and CHK-002 verificationEvidence — HIGH: the ratified contract requires a post-implementation matrix on at least two real hosts and explicitly says pre-implementation document reviews do not count, while every CHK-002 real-host/child-shell intent is marked satisfied only by deterministic story-owner-lease/guardrail/CLI smokes. Those tests exercise synthetic env objects, not actual Codex/Claude/Antigravity launcher propagation or nested child shells, so host-specific env loss and source/provider drift remain untested. Run and bind fresh post-implementation real-host transcripts (at least two providers, plus one degraded ppid negative) or keep the affected intents/checklist incomplete.

packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:8-16 and 68-134 persist generated tokens with createdAt but implement no expiry, ownership-scoped cleanup, or enumeration; handlers/doctor.ts only reports the current resolved identity and does not expose token-store cleanup/health. This conflicts with the ratified contract at owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:242-245 and R3:386-390, and with B-62b8 decision pre-mortem #3. WHY: generated fallback state can accumulate indefinitely and the documented ownership/cleanup boundary is not actually delivered. Add a bounded cleanup policy plus doctor visibility without raw dimensions or tokens, and tests proving one task-role cannot delete or reuse another pair token.

docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:54-73,290-298,445-456 promise that lifecycle events consume the opaque shared canonical resolver and never persist raw host task/session tokens, but packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1132-1135 and 1191-1195 still write process.env.LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SESSION directly into both the activity log and story process-events; packages/main/src/init-assets.ts:360-365 populates that variable from raw CODEX_SESSION_ID/OPENAI_SESSION_ID/TERM_SESSION_ID. HIGH: an ordinary Codex launch can therefore leak a raw host token into logs/story metadata and retains a second session source of truth outside the resolver, while the guardrail does not match LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SESSION. Route both event writers through getSessionIdentity()/the opaque canonical id, preserve source/provider only as diagnostics, and add a sentinel regression proving raw native values never reach either artifact.

packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:72-77,100-120 and 321-345 impose an absolute seven-day expiry from createdAt and never refresh last-use/expiry for an active task-role pair. Repro on current build: resolve one generated token at 2026-01-01, reuse at 2026-01-07T23:59:59 (same), then resolve at 2026-01-08T00:00:01 (different). WHY: a still-active long-running task silently rotates its owner identity and can be rejected by its own fresh owner lease, recreating the exact cross-invocation self-lock this story fixes. Make cleanup idle-based or otherwise prove an actively used pair cannot rotate while it can still own/refresh a lease; retain bounded cleanup for genuinely abandoned scopes and add the expiry-boundary regression.

packages/main/src/core/lattice-dispatch.ts:1682-1684 — HIGH: F-002 remains bypassable because the new deny check uses raw Array.includes while buildRequiredCommandEnv normalizes deny names with trim(). With envAllowlist=[LATTICE_SESSION_ID] and envDenylist=[" LATTICE_SESSION_ID "], current dist propagates must-stay-denied; the canonical env builder had already removed it. Normalize the deny set once and reuse it (and add whitespace-deny regression), otherwise deny precedence is inconsistent across the same policy.

packages/main/src/core/owner-session-token-store.ts:317-374 and docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md:248-254 — HIGH: the fixed seven-day expiresAt rotates a generated owner id even when the same adapter task/role is still active. Executable repro: create the scoped token at t0, acquire a lease with it, resolve again at t0+TTL+1, then invoke acquireOrRefresh from the new id; TOKEN_ROTATED=true and the active lease result is foreign. A long-running task therefore deterministically self-locks every seven days, recreating the exact owner-identity failure this story is meant to remove. Expiry must be renewed/sliding while the scope is live, or cleanup must prove the token is no longer bound to an active lease before rotation.

packages/main/src/tasks/story-owner-lease-smoke.ts:581-595 — HIGH: the new degraded-mutation regression invokes checklist_update against the live B-62b8 story, so it is phase-dependent. It passes only in DEV; in current REVIEW (and later TEST) command policy rejects checklist_update before owner-lease acquisition, producing no degraded warning and failing the smoke assertion. Confirmed by npm --prefix packages/main run test:story-owner-lease-smoke in REVIEW. This will deterministically break routine/full validation outside DEV. Use an isolated fixture/state whose phase permits the mutation or a phase-neutral owner-gated seam, and assert both pre-mutation warning and foreign rejection there.

packages/main/src/tasks/story-owner-lease-smoke.ts:754-774 — HIGH incomplete F-005 repair: the new focused regression is lifecycle-state-dependent and fails in the current REVIEW phase. Repro: `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/main run test:story-owner-lease-smoke` fails at line 774 because the spawned `checklist_update` is rejected by the REVIEW phase policy before owner-lease enforcement; stderr contains `Command checklist_update is not available in REVIEW phase`, so no degraded pre-mutation warning is emitted. The new child identity/race/real session_brief/doctor cases at lines 584-752 are useful and independently cover those slices, but no spawned composite actually acquires then refreshes the same lease across different parent-process shapes; later lease refresh cases still run under explicit `sess-alpha`. Checklist evidence also remains the old a175883c blanket command/note citing unchanged `cli-surface-smoke` rather than the new a2f141b9 child-process suite, so it still overstates the bound proof. WHY: a regression that passes only while the story is in DEV becomes a deterministic REVIEW/TEST/full-suite blocker and does not prove the original cross-process owner refresh. Make the pre-mutation check phase-independent using a bounded temporary story/project or child-mode lease choke point, add two spawned same-composite acquire/refresh invocations with heartbeat/no-foreign assertions, rerun in REVIEW, and rebind affected evidence to the exact new command and claims.
